edits.current:
An alias-named generic record can retain a closed value argument in its
`provenance.arguments` without exposing that argument as a host field. The
compiler emits `{kind: "value", type, value}` for canonical `Nat`, `Bool`, and
`String` indices: unbounded unsigned decimal, `true`/`false`, or exact
Unicode-scalar text. Reviewed Binding IR must restate both the primitive kind
and value exactly. Open or opaque values and other index types fail at the Lean
argument; no adapter infers an index from a host representation. The alias
continues to supply the public nominal identity and its runtime payload fields.

edits.previous: Closed natural-number indices use aliases such as `abbrev Triple := Sized 3`, where `Sized` stores `data : Array Nat` and a proof `data.size = n`. A checked constructor takes `data` and returns `Option Triple`. The host record has only `data`; the index `3` remains in authenticated type metadata. A package can export only `Nat → Triple` without having a checked input anywhere.

edits.current:
The compiler and reviewed contract admit three canonical index kinds: an unbounded `Nat`, `Bool`, and `String`. They are serialized as unsigned decimal, `true`/`false`, and exact Unicode-scalar text respectively; zero, the empty string, and supplementary characters are valid. Lean reduces a closed expression before recording it, so `1 + 2` and `decide (1 < 2)` become `3` and `true`. Open or opaque values are rejected. `Int`, `Char`, fixed-width or platform-width integers, `Fin`, functions, proofs, instances, and other index types require a separately reviewed representation and are not inferred from a host value. The installed package archives below currently exercise closed `Nat` indices; the broader installed rollout remains separately tracked.

For a reviewed API, record erased proof names in the type's `lean-lang.org/erased-proofs` extension, and select `{ "kind": "checked-record", "constructor": "CheckedRecords.mkInterval" }` in the declaration's parameter refinement. A closed index appears in `lean-lang.org/instantiation` as `{ "kind": "value", "type": { "kind": "primitive", "name": "nat" }, "value": "3" }`, with `name` and `value` changed to `bool` plus `true`/`false`, or `string` plus the exact text. The [independent review fixture](../../tests/helpers/checked-record-fixture.mjs) shows the complete forms. Fresh Lean must reproduce the payload layout, erased names, index kind and value, and selected constructor. Changing or omitting an instantiation constraint fails reconciliation. Configuration contracts cannot override a review.

edits.previous: For a record whose proofs relate its fields, use a [checked constructor over the payload fields](existing-package.md#export-a-record-with-proof-fields). The host supplies no proof. The compiler checks each input through the selected Lean constructor and erases proofs from Lean-produced results. Closed `Nat` indices stay in type metadata. They cover direct and repeated parameters, arrays, lists, options, products, `Except`/`Result`, enclosing record fields, active variant fields and constructor-free container results. [Installed inherited checked-record acceptance](../evidence/inherited-checked-record-promotion-20261018.md) additionally covers the tested acyclic `Span → Ticket → Stamped` chain, with independently selected parent and child constructors and proof-free results. Select the record constructor and each nested checked field's constructor independently at every public input site; only an active variant branch runs. Generic or recursive checked records, value-carrying receiver-dependent inherited fields, callback, owned and open dependent combinations remain unfinished.

edits.current:
for argument in args, position in [0:args.size] do
          let inferredArgumentType ← inferType argument
          let argumentType ← whnf inferredArgumentType
          unless argumentType.isSort do
            -- A value index is recorded only as instantiation provenance. Canonical strings keep
            -- arbitrary-size Nat literals exact, distinguish both Bool constructors and preserve
            -- Unicode String contents without turning any index into a host-visible field.
            if ← isProp inferredArgumentType then
              reject argument "generic record value arguments cannot be proofs"
            if parameterBinders[position]! == .instImplicit || (← isClass? inferredArgumentType).isSome then
              reject argument "generic record value arguments cannot be typeclass instances"
            if argumentType.isForall then
              reject argument "generic record value arguments cannot be functions"
            let normalized ← whnf argument
            let (indexType, index) ←
              if ← isDefEq argumentType (mkConst ``Nat) then
                let .lit (.natVal value) := normalized
                  | reject argument "generic record Nat value arguments must be closed literals"
                pure (mkConst ``Nat, toString value)
              else if ← isDefEq argumentType (mkConst ``Bool) then
                match normalized with
                | .const ``Bool.false [] => pure (mkConst ``Bool, "false")
                | .const ``Bool.true [] => pure (mkConst ``Bool, "true")
                | _ => reject argument "generic record Bool value arguments must be closed literals"
              else if ← isDefEq argumentType (mkConst ``String) then
                let .lit (.strVal value) := normalized
                  | reject argument "generic record String value arguments must be closed literals"
                pure (mkConst ``String, value)
              else
                reject argument "generic record value arguments must have type Nat, Bool or String"
